All I can say is WOW... so Just like this game I had AI write me a review for it 
"1/10 STEAM PEAK PLAYERS PER GAME (AND THAT'S ONE TOO MANY)
The Girl In White
Played: 1 hour (then refunded faster than the dev's career)
Buckle up, folks—this is peak "Hot Garbage Games" material. "The Girl In White" promises high-school romance, ghost-busting dreams, turn-based dungeons, and "bizarre personality quizzes." What it delivers? A dumpster fire so hot, it makes asset flips look like Elden Ring.
Store page screams scam from jump: AI-generated title screen and cutscenes (they admit it!), zero screenshots that show actual gameplay, no trailer. Description rips off every generic JRPG trope—dream corridors? Wandering spirits? Loot "questionable gear"? Bro, this ain't innovative; it's ChatGPT on bath salts.
Launch day: Nov 12, 2025. All-time peak players? 1. Current? 0. Followers? Laughable 27. Reviews? Zilch. In 6 weeks, not a soul cared enough to drop feedback. Dev Succubella Games (solo outfit, natch) slapped this BabylonJS web-port slop on Steam, jacked it to $8, then "discounted" to $2 'cause no one bites full price on vaporware.
Gameplay? Turn-based "dungeon crawling" that's just mashing through empty hallways with placeholder enemies. Quizzes? Absurdity levels off the charts—think "What's your spirit animal: A) Ghost B) Broke dev." Combat crashes your potato PC (min specs from 2007, but runs like 1997). Story? High schooler sees ghosts, falls in "love"—ends in 45 mins if you don't ragequit. Free DLC "Afterstory"? Probably just a .txt file saying "Thanks for the $2."
Refunded in 12 mins flat. Valve, nuke this. Dev, stick to AI waifu generators.
TL;DR: 1 player peak = 1 too many. Pure Steam landfill fodder."
